desc:
A paragraph consists of words in a fixed order; lens[i] is the length of word i. The words are placed on lines of width characters in the given order, and neighbouring words on the same line are separated by exactly one space. A line must not be longer than width, and a word is never split across lines.

For every line except the last one, the penalty is (width - lineLength)2, where lineLength counts the letters plus the spaces. The last line has no penalty. Return the smallest total penalty over all valid ways to break the paragraph into lines.

lens = [3,2,2,5], width = 6  -> 10   (lines: [3], [2,2], [5] gives 9 + 1 + 0)
lens = [4,4,4],   width = 4  -> 0    (one word per line, all lines are exactly full)
hints: A greedy rule such as 'put as many words on each line as fit' can be beaten: sometimes moving one word to the next line makes both lines better. Think about the position where the last line ends.
Let dp[i] be the least penalty to place the first i words so that line i ends exactly after word i-1. The last line of that prefix starts at some word j.

dp[i] = min over valid j of dp[j] + cost(j, i), where the line made of words j..i-1 must fit in width, and the cost is (width - length)^2 unless i equals the total number of words (then the cost is 0). A line holds at most about width / 2 words, so for each i you only need to look back that far.
editorial: Let dp[i] be the smallest penalty for the first i words, where word i-1 ends a line. The last line of this prefix contains words j .. i-1 for some j, and it is valid when sum(lens[j..i-1]) + (i - 1 - j) ≤ width. Its cost is (width - length)2, except for the very last line of the whole paragraph (i = n), which is free. Then dp[i] = min(dp[j] + cost) over the valid j, and the answer is dp[n].

Scan j downward from i - 1 while keeping the running line length, and stop as soon as the line gets too long. Because every word has length at least 1, a line contains at most (width + 1) / 2 words, so the whole DP is O(n · width) time with O(n) memory. Every word fits on a line of its own, so dp[j] is always finite.
solution:
def minRaggedness(lens, width):
    n = len(lens)
    INF = float("inf")
    dp = [INF] * (n + 1)
    dp[0] = 0
    for i in range(1, n + 1):
        total = -1
        best = INF
        for j in range(i - 1, -1, -1):
            total += lens[j] + 1
            if total > width:
                break
            cost = 0 if i == n else (width - total) ** 2
            v = dp[j] + cost
            if v < best:
                best = v
        dp[i] = best
    return dp[n]
